previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with end-stage renal disease, a functioning pancreatic transplant, mechanical mitral valve on anticoagulation, and systolic heart failure was admitted for fever, nausea, and vomiting. She was transferred from an outside hospital where she received antibiotics and imaging showed gallbladder wall thickening and stranding around a failed renal graft. Evaluation revealed no acute cholecystitis on ultrasound and no source of bacterial infection; blood cultures were negative. Her symptoms resolved, and liver enzymes normalized, consistent with a viral syndrome. Her INR was supratherapeutic at 6.6, peaking at 10, prompting administration of vitamin K. INR stabilized at 2.9, and warfarin was restarted at 5 mg daily. She underwent one session of hemodialysis, which improved her renal function and overall stability. She was discharged home with instructions to monitor INR, resume her regular dialysis schedule, and follow up with her primary care and transplant teams.
